festivals.what: Yi Peng, the Lanna (northern Thai) form of Loi Krathong, is held on the full moon of the 12th Thai lunar month, usually in November. Lanterns hang outside homes and temples, sky lanterns (khom loi) are released, and there are street parades. TAT says guidelines are set on the times and places where sky lanterns may be released; check that year's Chiang Mai provincial notice before releasing one.
Yi Peng 2026: the main full-moon night is reported as Tuesday 24 November 2026, with celebrations over about three to four days around it. Not yet confirmed from a Thai government page.

Songkran (Thai New Year) runs longer in Chiang Mai than the national 13 to 15 April holiday, often from 12 to 16 April. In 2026 the Chiang Mai Water Festival was held 11 to 13 April at Wat Chedi Luang; at Wat Phra Sing, scented water is poured over elders' hands as a blessing.

closures: Sky lanterns and aircraft: for Loi Krathong 2024 the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand warned pilots of lantern releases within 20 nautical miles (about 37 km) of Chiang Mai International Airport, covering parts of Chiang Mai and Lamphun, in set evening windows on 15 and 16 November.
moving_calendars: Yi Peng and Loi Krathong: full moon of the 12th Thai lunar month (re-dated each year).
culture-cycles.note: Yi Peng lantern times and no-release areas are set each year by the province; the 2026 notice was not found. The 2026 date is a signal only.
